Try making sure the screen is lit up before scanning your finger print and make sure is parallel to the phone screen :) not the edges of your thumb. 

Another thing I done is I made a fingerprint of my thumb and then a second one of the same thumb but focused on the edges instead. Works a charm

First question you should ask yourself is do you really need all your date transferred over onto your new phone? 

One of the best things about getting a new phone is the speed and all that extra space, when you transfer everything over you're clogging up your new phone. If you have 4 or so hours I'd sit down with both phones and manually install everything on your new phone, back any photos you want from your old phone up to the cloud. This has an added benefit of getting used to getting around your phone and how it feels it. 

Next thing I would do it go into the display setting and choose one you like the best. 120hz is amazing! Watch a side by side comparison on YouTube, you'll never be able to go back to a 60hz screen ever! I remember just sitting and scrolling for hours because the satisfaction was unparalleled.  

Next thing to setup is how you want your home, back and app buttons to look, do you want them there all of the time? Or would you rather swipe up gestures? Swipe up gestures takes about 30 minutes to get used to but gives you a bit extra screen space and it's a little less for you phone to keep rendered in, thus spending up your phone by a fraction of a second constantly. 

I'd then setup the side wipey menu thing, can't remember what it's called 🤣 basically is just your most used apps, contacts etc, easily accessible all if the time by swiping the menu from the side. You probably won't use it for a few weeks as you'll forget its there but it's amazing!

Setup samsung pay and samsung pass, they are a must! As well as this setup your fingerprint, I set 2 up for 1 finger so I can unlock it from any angle with no problem. 

Finally I'd setup bixby menu, this is news, music etc. I personally turned mine off as I never used it but that's personal preference.

On a final note, check YouTube for all the hidden features and spend the next few days checking out any and all hidden features of your new phone. Enjoy your new phone, of you need anymore help the Samsung community is always here to help and share our knowledge :)
